scenario: Connect an existing no-argument function to Set Timer by Event on self or an explicit object endpoint; preview, edit, repeat, replace, undo, tidy, capture and compile.

findings: Repeated identical binding creates another node and dirties the asset.
Replacement result omits the displaced source identity.

limitations: Synthetic timer-delegate scenario; not all delegate signatures or object classes.
Runtime registration requires execution of the owning node; creation alone does not register the delegate.
Explicit-object test uses a Self node; distinct runtime instances, external class callbacks and every signature were not exercised.
No runtime timer firing or save/reload claim.
Schema callback failures and partial rollback restoration were source-reviewed, not exhaustively fault-injected.
Existing source nodes are retained on replacement; cleanup is deliberately separate.
visual_review: Inspected native capture: clear execution line and forward Self -> Create Event -> Set Timer connections, selected OnTimer function visible, no overlapping nodes.
fixes: Return unchanged before probing when the same compatible function/object is already connected.
Identify replaced input sources and retain their nodes for explicit inspection; accurately distinguish an empty input.
Require explicit K2 graph, valid existing connection and safe proposed coordinates.
Clarify function binding versus runtime registration, parameter help, side effects, layout and explicit compile/save.
